In situ spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) reveal that surface F species serve as hydrogen‐bond acceptors that reconfigure the interfacial water network, enhancing K + enrichment, local alkalinity, CO 2 accumulation, and rapid proton transfer. Density functional theory (DFT) further indicates that F‐Bi surface, combined with the K + /H 2 O microenvironment, facilitates charge redistribution, enhances *CO 2 and *OCHO adsorption, and then lowers the reaction energy barrier. This work overcomes the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade‐off in CO 2 electrolysis, offering a promising strategy for designing high‐performance pH‐universal electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Pre‐Organized Active Sites Strategy Steering a Bismuth‐Based MOF Nanosheet for High‐Efficiency Acidic CO2 Electroreduction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to formic acid in acidic media offers a promising route to mitigate carbon loss, yet it remains challenging to design catalysts that effectively suppress the competing hydrogen evolution reaction and achieve industrial‐level current densities under acidic conditions. Here, we demonstrate exfoliating a densely packed 3D pillar‐layered bismuth‐based metal–organic framework into ultrathin nanosheets, enabling efficient CO 2 ‐to‐formic acid conversion. Remarkably, the removal of 1,4‑benzenedicarboxylate linkers during exfoliation leads to the exposure of the underlying dinuclear bismuth sites, which retain the original coordination site geometry. Mechanistic studies reveal that these exposed dinuclear sites exhibit intrinsic geometric compatibility with key intermediates (*CO 2 or *OCHO), resembling the native carboxylate binding mode, thereby significantly lowering the Gibbs free energy barrier for intermediate formation. Concurrently, the modified electronic structure results in a reduced work function that facilitates electron transfer. As a result, the optimized catalyst achieves an industrial‐relevant current density of 500 mA cm −2 with a formic acid Faradaic efficiency of 95%, doubling the performance of the bulk MOF and surpassing most reported catalysts. This work highlights a precise structural evolution strategy for creating geometrically optimized active sites, offering new insights into the design of efficient electrocatalysts for acidic CO 2 reduction.

papers.title: Regulating Surface Electron Dynamics Enables Selective C─N Coupling in Photoelectrochemical Oxime Synthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A central challenge in photoelectrochemical multi‐electron transformations is simultaneously achieving efficient charge separation and precise control over reaction selectivity. Herein, we construct a p–n junction photocathode composed of an atomic‐layer‐deposited ZnO x layer and black silicon (b‐Si) to regulate interfacial electron dynamics and reaction selectivity. Upon illumination, oxygen vacancies in the ZnO x surface serve as electron‐buffering sites that facilitate reversible charge storage and release, as confirmed by in situ Kelvin probe force microscopy. This modulation of electron chemical potential suppresses competing hydrogen evolution and over‐reduction pathways, while directing nitrogen‐centered intermediates toward selective hydroxylamine formation and subsequent C─N coupling. The optimized photocathode delivers a photocurrent density of 38.6 mA cm −2 with a Faradaic efficiency of 94.6% for cyclohexanone oxime production and a cyclohexanone‐to‐oxime selectivity of 99.9%. Mechanistic studies combining operando spectroscopy, density functional theory, and microkinetic analysis reveal that coverage‐dependent site competition governs surface site availability, thereby inhibiting the further reduction of hydroxylamine and promoting its desorption for solution‐phase coupling. Integration of the microkinetic model with the photovoltaic response establishes a quantitative design principle based on the matching between semiconductor photoresponse and interfacial catalytic kinetics, providing a general framework for selectivity control in photoelectrochemical systems.

papers.title: A Polycatenane‑Topological Covalent Organic Polymer for High‑Performance Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The introduction of polycatenane junctions into dative B←N bond‐linked covalent organic polymers (COPs) poses a significant synthetic challenge for the synergistic optimization of both geometric stabilization and molecular functionality. Herein, we strategically employ tritopic borate ligands bearing terminal –Br substituents, rather than their ditopic counterparts, as precursors to construct a single‐crystalline COP ( JNP‐7 ) featuring polycatenane‐like topological junctions. Specifically, B‐centered Lewis acceptors and N‐donor units initially assemble into 1D nanoribbons via dative B←N linkages. By leveraging inter‐nanoribbon halogen···halogen interactions between the semi‐interlocked Br‐containing motifs, the architecture is further extended into 2D arrays, thereby elevating the geometric dimensionality of JNP‐7 . Critically, the resulting polycatenated halogen‐bonded network imparts exceptional structural rigidity, and the dative B←N motifs are found to concurrently promote visible‐light harvesting and facilitate charge‐carrier migration. Consequently, JNP‐7 enables highly efficient H 2 O 2 production via both the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and water oxidation reaction (WOR) under ambient sunlight, operating without sacrificial agents, photosensitizers, or metal cocatalysts, and outperforming state‐of‐the‐art covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) in terms of photocatalytic activity and apparent quantum yield (AQY). By aligning molecular topology with catalytic function, this work establishes a generalizable framework for the rational development of topologically sophisticated, high‐performance COP systems.

papers.title: Tailored sp2‐C─F Bonding for Reversible Oxygen‐Peroxide Electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable zinc‐air batteries are fundamentally limited by the sluggishness of four‐electron (4e − ) oxygen electrocatalysis and by bifunctional catalysts that rarely combine high activity with long‐term durability, resulting in substantial polarization and poor reversibility. Replacing this chemistry with O 2 –H 2 O 2 interconversion offers a compelling alternative, because two‐electron (2e − ) oxygen electrocatalysis features intrinsically more reversible pathways and faster kinetics. Herein, fluorine‐doped graphene is established as a programmable electrocatalytic platform for O 2 ‐H 2 O 2 interconversion, where tailored sp 2 ‐C─F bonding acts as a precise electronic lever to regulate OOH* intermediate binding and thereby steer O 2 –H 2 O 2 redox selectivity and kinetics. By controlling fluorine incorporation, the local electronic environment of graphene is delicately engineered without sacrificing electrical conductivity. The optimized catalyst exhibits outstanding bifunctional activity for 2e − oxygen reduction reaction (2e – ‐ORR) and peroxide oxidation reaction (POR), translating into rechargeable zinc‐based batteries with high power output and robust long‐term durability. Mechanistic studies reveal that sp 2 ‐C─F bonding induces localized electrostatic polarization at neighboring carbon sites, selectively stabilizing OOH* intermediates, lowering the kinetic barrier for 2e – ‐ORR, and concurrently facilitating POR while minimizing parasitic reactions. These findings demonstrate a fundamental structure‐property principle linking fluorine‐induced polarization with O 2 –H 2 O 2 redox kinetics, and position fluorinated carbon frameworks as a versatile foundation for next‐generation reversible energy storage.

Heterostructure-engineered C3N5/C3N4 nanohybrid with efficient photocatalytic performance for hydrogen production
papers.abstract: Visible light photocatalytic water splitting offers a sustainable pathway for green hydrogen production, yet rapid charge-carrier recombination remains a major limitation of carbon nitride photocatalysts. Here, we report an all-carbon-nitride S-scheme heterojunction constructed from two stoichiometrically distinct yet structurally related semiconductors, C 3 N 4 and C 3 N 5 . Their contrasting electronic structures provide complementary band energetics: C 3 N 4 possesses a wider bandgap and more negative conduction-band potential, whereas C 3 N 5 exhibits a narrower bandgap and more positive valence-band potential, enabling extended visible-light harvesting while retaining strong redox capability. The structural integrity and intimate interfacial coupling of the two carbon nitride phases were confirmed by NMR and NEXAFS analysis. The UPS measurements, supported by EPR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, reveal that Fermi-level equilibration upon heterojunction formation induces interfacial charge redistribution, band bending and an internal electric field that drives directional S-scheme charge transfer. The developed C 3 N 5 /C 3 N 4 nanohybrid achieves an excellent hydrogen generation of 749 µmol h -1 g -1 , significantly outperforming individual components. The enhanced activity originates from the synergistic combination of favourable band alignment, efficient interfacial charge separation and preserved redox potentials. These findings establish stoichiometry-driven interfacial electronic engineering within structurally related carbon nitrides as a powerful strategy for constructing efficient, metal-free S-scheme photocatalysts for solar hydrogen production.

papers.title: Synergistic Interactions Enable Superior Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity in Compositionally Complex Nanocrystal–Nanosheet Hybrids
papers.abstract: Abstract Thiospinel nanoparticles are promising catalytic materials due to their compositional tunability, electronic conductivity, and structural stability. While significant gains in catalysis have been made through material engineering, one continuously developing route is through the use of support materials to enhance performance. Here, we report a simple, scalable, low-temperature method to coproduce colloidal multimetal nanocrystals (<20 nm in diameter) and In2S3-based nanosheets (<1 nm thick), forming compositionally complex hybrid nanocrystal–nanosheet heterostructures in situ. The in situ-formed heterostructures demonstrate enhanced catalytic activity in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline conditions; peak performance was achieved in heterostructures formed between (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals and (In,Fe,Mn)2S3 nanosheets with overpotentials as low as 283 mV at 10 mA/cm2. Heterostructures can also be produced ex situ by introducing nanosheets, postsynthetically, to the nanocrystals, reducing the overpotential of (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals from 362 mV to 312 mV with only a 5 wt % addition. This improvement highlights synergistic interactions in the heterostructures. These results suggest that an optimum nanosheet loading that maximizes effective nanocrystal–nanosheet interfacial coupling while preserving access to the Ni/Co-rich catalytic domains is the relevant design parameter. Our findings provide a low-temperature, colloidal route for synthesizing compositionally complex and highly uniform (<15% dispersity) sulfide nanocrystals, nanosheets, or heterostructures of the two with tunable structures and enhanced electrocatalytic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a compositionally complex hybrid material that is able to enhance performance when formed both in situ or ex situ and the use of In2S3 as a scaffold for a support material for enhancing OER performance.

papers.title: Cation‐Anion Co‐Adsorption With Facet‐Preferential Tendency for Stable Wide‐Temperature Zinc‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) face critical challenges from dendrite growth, side reactions, and polyiodide shuttling at the zinc anode, particularly under extreme temperatures. This work presents a dual‐ion synergistic interfacial regulation strategy with Facet‐Preferential Tendency enabled by a trace ammonium iodide (NH 4 I) additive. Iodide ions (I − ), as soft bases, exhibit a facet‐preferential adsorption preference for Zn surfaces to guide uniform Zn 2+ deposition, while ammonium ions (NH 4 + ) are enriched at the Zn(101) facet and tip sites to provide electrostatic shielding and homogenize the electric field. Moreover, the adsorbed NH 4 + cations effectively capture free polyiodide anions via electrostatic interaction, suppressing their conversion into detrimental I 2 and mitigating the shuttle effect. This facet‐preferential complementary adsorption constructs a low‐polarization interphase that simultaneously suppresses hydrogen evolution, blocks water contact, and accelerates Zn 2+ transport. Consequently, the Zn//PANI(Polyaniline) full cell retains 90.05% capacity after a record 70 000 cycles at −30°C. Critically, practical Zn/I 2 pouch cells with a high‐loading cathode deliver a capacity retention of 85.53% after 900 cycles at 2 C under −30°C. This work breaks the low‐temperature performance bottleneck and provides a rational, practical design principle for long‐life aqueous batteries in extreme climates.

papers.title: Electronic Modulation via Dual‐Phase Coupling of CoNi Alloy and NiCo2S4 on N, S‐Co‐Doped Porous Carbon Spheres for High‐Performance Rechargeable Zn‐Air Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of efficient bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts for rechargeable Zn‐air batteries remains constrained by the trade‐off between activity and durability. Here, we break this bottleneck by rationally constructing a CoNi alloy/NiCo 2 S 4 dual‐phase heterostructure embedded in N, S‐codoped porous carbon spheres (CoNi/NiCo 2 S 4 @NSPCs) via controlled partial sulfidation. Crucially, this mild process partially converts CoNi nanoparticles into NiCo 2 S 4 , preserving the highly conductive alloy phase while creating intimately coupled metal/sulfide heterointerfaces. The resulting architecture synergistically combines alloy conductivity, abundant sulfide active sites, and efficient mass transport through the porous carbon framework. Density functional theory(DFT) calculations reveal that interfacial electronic redistribution optimizes oxygen‐intermediate adsorption, thereby accelerating both oxygen reduction reaction(ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction(OER) kinetics. Consequently, the catalyst achieves outstanding bifunctional performance with a low overpotential gap and remarkable operational stability. When employed as an air‐cathode catalyst, CoNi/NiCo 2 S 4 @NSPCs enables a flexible Zn‐air battery (FZAB) with an open‐circuit voltage of 1.44 V and a high specific capacity of 656.77 mAh g Zn −1 , while maintaining stable charge–discharge operation under bending and over 100 h of cycling. These metrics surpass most state‐of‐the‐art bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. This work establishes partial sulfidation as a general strategy for engineering dual‐phase nonprecious metal electrocatalysts for practical flexible energy applications.
